content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Sick absences are far above normal on both queues: 9 on general against about 2.4 usual, and 7 on payments against about 2.6 usual. Most notes say 'Called in sick - fever', logged between 07:00 and 08:55. That leaves general at 51 agents against 57.6 expected (-11%). Demand is not the issue: volumes are 7–15% below forecast, handle times are at or below forecast, and there are no incidents or campaigns. Service level is still 100% because of the light early volume, but the staffing gap will bite as volume ramps into the late-morning peak.","plan_name":"Backfill general for sick absences through the midday peak","rationale":"General is short about 6–7 agents for the day. Cancelling non-mandatory coaching on general returns agents to the phones at low cost. Two consecutive overtime offers of 8 agents each are expected to bring roughly 3 extra agents for the 10:00–14:00 peak, at about Rs 4,600, well within the Rs 15,000 budget. Agents arrive 30 minutes after approval, so offers approved now cover a 10:00 start. Payments is also running thin from sickness, so moving cross-skilled agents from it is not advisable. Its service level is 100% and volume is below forecast, so no spend is needed there yet; it should be watched. Callback and deflection are held back because demand is normal.
